subject: Fraud & Scams
title: Ferdinand Demara: The Great Impostor
description: A fast breakdown of Ferdinand Demara: The Great Impostor for builders.

hook.text: Ferdinand Demara impersonated a surgeon and successfully performed operations on wounded soldiers.

buildup.text: He also posed as a prison warden, a monk, a professor, and a civil engineer.

discovery.text: Demara studied textbooks hours before performing procedures. His patients actually survived.

twist.text: He wasn't motivated by money — he simply wanted to be important. Most of his roles were unpaid.

climax.text: His story became a 1961 film. He was never convicted because most institutions were too embarrassed.

punchline.text: He operated on soldiers. None of them died. He wasn't a doctor.

quiz.question: What made Ferdinand Demara unusual among con artists?
options: He wasn't motivated by money — he wanted importance
